chapter_title: Concerning the Twelve Signs of the Zodiac and the

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
Whether it is the whole arrangement of general governing influences fixed in the outermost plane, or the sufficient set of dominant impulses that move through that arrangement, all of them are ruling powers, each acting from its own quality. They are mutually hostile and rivalrous, with one pressing down another and each threatening the rest. They take from one another through the operation of the ordering power that has formed all states into a coherent system. That ordering power has gathered these influences, bound them in the outermost degree within a continually recurring cycle; and as that cycle turns and drives their alternations, they carry out whatever their ruling loves crave, in inner and outer life, according to their delight. Yet above them there is a restraining oversight and superior exaction that compels them, draws from them what is due, and takes away what they would seize as their own.

This is the right way to understand the structure. These ruling tendencies were seized out of a full series of fundamental evils and falsities and fixed into the outermost cycle, and from each fundamental origin a paired determination was taken so that every kind of perversion might have a place in the general governance. From obscured understanding that feigns intelligence came the twin power of divided reasoning and confident persuasion. From the burning of self-love came the power of initiating from self and the power of domineering over others. From volatile persuasion that disturbs discernment came the power of possessive craving, the power of self-justifying balance, and the power of casting truths into mere opinion. From falsified truth that should have been living came the power of enclosing affection within appearances, the power of separating purity from charity, and the power of immersing the mind in fluctuating pretense. From active denial of good came the power of hard restraint and the power of secret malice. These are the complete set of ruling depraved tendencies, by which wickedness is kept in motion and not allowed to cease, because they bring forth every disorder in the human mind and in its effects, whether the disorder appears in perception or in act.

Understand also the chief leaders among these influences, the more immediate dominant impulses: the impulse of self-derived counsel and proud reasoning arose from obscured understanding; the impulse of alluring delight arose from the burning of self-love; the impulse of contention and assault arose from volatile persuasion; the impulse of subtle calculation and shifting interpretation arose from falsified truth; and the impulse of cold resistance and despairing constraint arose from active denial of good.

Also, two chief determinations are counted with burning love turned into craving: one mode that hardens into resistance, and another that yields into appetite. These two act as a generative pair for the whole, as a kind of father and mother for these perversions.

Also, higher governing principles were numbered among them in the rule of the arrangement so that the whole might be held under superior governance. It can be perceived that these higher governing principles continually subjugate the depraved influences at every moment.

These seven—those five chief impulses together with the two generative determinations—are the operative powers of evil that bring about every wicked and corrupt act throughout the whole extent of life, in inner and outer things, within every affection and thought, in what is resistant and what is receptive, in perception and in deed.

Again, the general governing influences are arranged into a complete distribution in the outermost plane: they are appointed to four quarters, three to each quarter, and fixed within the recurring cycle of external life. The group that springs from self-initiating pride, domineering ambition, and confident persuasion stands in one quarter; the group that springs from possessive craving, hard restraint, and the separation of purity from charity stands in another; the group that springs from divided reasoning, self-justifying balance, and casting truths into mere opinion stands in another; and the group that springs from secret malice, fluctuating pretense, and enclosing affection within appearances stands in the remaining quarter. Thus the whole is set in fourfold completeness, distributed through the outermost cycle.

Therefore, when the quarter governed by self-initiating pride, domineering ambition, and confident persuasion is forcibly exacted and stripped by the restraining oversight above it, together with the chief impulses active there, then immediately disorder strikes the lower affections of the natural mind. When the quarter governed by possessive craving, the separation of purity from charity, and hard restraint is forcibly exacted, then disorder at once befalls elementary perceptions and their derivative knowledges, together with the uses and works that proceed from them. When the quarter governed by secret malice, fluctuating pretense, and enclosing affection within appearances is forcibly exacted, then there is scarcity of living truth in outer life and a drying up of understanding from one state to another. Conversely, when the quarter governed by divided reasoning, self-justifying balance, and casting truths into mere opinion is forcibly exacted, then distortion and diminishment befall the form of human will and thought as it comes forth into life, varying from one state to another.

Now it has been made plain concerning the full set of these general governing depraved influences: they were formed out of the series of fundamental evils and falsities and fixed into the outermost cycle.

It has also been made plain concerning the other five chief impulses: they too arose from those same fundamental origins of denial and perversion.

It has also been made plain concerning the two generative determinations: they belong to the hidden activity of craving in its resistant mode and in its yielding mode, acting as the generative pair.

And again it has been made plain concerning the higher governing principles: they are not of the same kind as these depraved influences; yet because the outermost plane must be held in order by what governs, and because whatever is present in the outermost plane receives determination by higher influx and is compelled to serve within bounds, they were numbered together in the external reckoning. For those higher governing principles are from a superior source of life and order, not arising from the depraved impulses or from the general perversions of the outermost cycle.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent as a single spiritual teaching: a system of depraved governing tendencies fixed in the outermost cycle under higher restraint, with a fivefold origin schema, a fivefold set of chief impulses, a twofold generative polarity, fourfold distribution, and observable effects when restraint exacts from each quarter. The main stumble is the forced specificity in mapping named lists to precise inner qualities, and the intrusive aside in ¶6, but the chapter largely reads as one consistent doctrinal voice.

findings.diagnosis: Coherent correspondential substrate. The passage teaches by function: cyclical constraint, mutual predation, and a superior exaction that limits them. No list-taxonomy pressure beyond the initial setup.
findings.evidence: Text teaches dynamics: “bound them on the sphere above, which circles constantly… so they shall do everything that they desire… Nevertheless, a guardian is over them, a debt-collector… compelling, extorting.” The spiritual reading did not stumble here; it could paraphrase the functional story (cyclic alternation + restraint) without forcing a mapping. This is what a clean substrate section looks like: the spiritual sense arises from what the powers *do* (oppress/plunder/are extorted), not from who administrates which station.

findings.diagnosis: Insertion/expansion of administrative taxonomy into a functional narrative. The ‘five worlds → zodiac assignments’ is governance-by-origin/jurisdiction rather than functional correspondence, and it produces the reader’s noted forced mappings (especially the irregular 2/2/3/3/2 distribution).
findings.evidence: The paragraph shifts from the functional account in ¶2 to a roster keyed to bureaucratic provenance: “Two zodiacal signs were taken per world… Gemini and Sagittarius belong to the world of smoke… Aries and Leo… Taurus, Aquarius and Libra… Cancer and Virgo and Pisces… Capricorn and Scorpio… These are the twelve rulers…” This is not argued by function (what Gemini *does*), but by allocation (“belong to”). The spiritual reading explicitly flags the strain: “The mapping… is forced by the list-structure; several determinations are interpretive (e.g., the threefold…).” That stumble is a classic sign of an imposed taxonomy at a seam: the narrative now requires symbolic guesswork to justify a list whose internal rationale is not in the substrate.
findings.scope: "They were [s]eized from the five worlds of Darkness, and bound on the sphere. Two zodiacal signs were taken per world. Gemini and Sagittarius belong to the world of smoke, which is the mind. In contrast, Aries and Leo belong to the world of fire. Taurus, Aquarius and Libra belong to the world of wind. Cancer and Virgo and [P]isces belong to the world of water. Capricorn and Scorpio belong to the world of Darkness."

findings.diagnosis: Administrative overlay block: the five planets are introduced as “leaders” and then allocated to the five dark worlds by origin (“generated from… belongs to…”). The spiritual reading reports the names have no functional role beyond filling a fivefold list, indicating a secondary systematizing layer.
findings.evidence: Text is pure provenance assignment: “the five stars, the leaders: from where were they formed? The star of Zeus… from the world of smoke… Aphrodite… from the world of fire… Ares… world of wind… Hermes… world of water… Cronos… world of Darkness.” The reader’s note matches the diagnostic: “The named planetary figures have no function here beyond ‘chief impulse’; their specific qualities are inferred from the fivefold origin list.” That is exactly governance/registry teaching (who comes from which realm), not correspondential teaching (what the star/force does and why that corresponds).
findings.scope: Annotate ¶4 as an administrative/provenance catalogue (five planetary rulers allocated to the five dark worlds), likely a systematizing overlay keyed to fivefold dark-world taxonomy.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty inside a mostly functional move. The “two ascendants… dry and moist… father and mother” can be read correspondentially (polarity generating effects), but the terminology is cryptic and invites interpretive substitution; this is not clearly an insertion because it continues the functional ‘generative pair’ logic and is not a named jurisdiction list.
findings.evidence: Unlike ¶3–4, ¶5 does not distribute named entities to territories; it states a functional polarity: “two ascendants… counted to fire and desire, the dry and the moist. They are the father and the mother of all these.” The spiritual reading’s stumble is lexical, not narrative: “rendered as resistant vs yielding… exact nuance uncertain.” Removing it would not improve flow; it supplies a mechanism (polarity generating the system) that fits ¶7’s “These seven…”.

findings.diagnosis: Damaged/marginal gloss intrusion inside the running text. The bracketed question-like aside (“but why did they count them in…?”) is a different discourse mode (reader/scribe questioning) and causes the spiritual reader’s noted ‘narrative intrusion.’ The underlying statement about counting sun and moon is coherent, but the embedded aside is not original continuous teaching.
findings.evidence: Text contains an explicit intrusive aside: “the sun and the moon… counted in with them as a rule ⟨[counte]d to their kind, but why did they count them in with them?⟩”. The spiritual reading flags it: “The text’s question-like aside… is a narrative intrusion.” That kind of parenthetical interrogative is typical of marginal scholion incorporated during copying/translation rather than Mani’s continuous didactic voice.
findings.scope: "⟨[counte]d to their kind, but why did they count them in with them?⟩"

findings.diagnosis: Coherent correspondential summary. It re-integrates the preceding items into functional causality (“doers of wickedness… do every wicked… in every creature”), which is substrate-style even if it relies on earlier catalogues.
findings.evidence: Functional universalization: “These seven… are the doers of wickedness that do every wicked and bad act… above and below… in every creature, in the dry and the moist, in tree and flesh.” The spiritual reading flows here without complaint; it is teaching by operation and scope, not by jurisdiction.

findings.diagnosis: Administrative distribution plus correspondential effect-claims: a mixed seam where a territorial/quadrant appointment list (administrative) is immediately used to explain effects in nature (correspondential). The reader’s stumble (“link… asserted rather than argued”) reflects the mechanical ‘when X quarter is plundered → Y category suffers’ schema: it is a governance model (guardian plunders a side) rather than a functional derivation.
findings.evidence: ¶8 is appointment language: “distributed, appointed on four sides, three per angle… placed like this, appointed… distributed.” ¶9 adds administrative actors: “plundered by the guardian who is over it… and the leaders who move upon it,” then asserts effects: “affliction strike… four-footed… herbs… scarcity… deformity… mankind.” The spiritual reading notes the weak internal rationale: “The assignment… rationale is not explicit” (¶8) and “link… is asserted rather than argued” (¶9). This is what happens when an administrative astrology schema (quarters/sides + guardian + leaders) is spliced onto an older correspondential interest in how disorder manifests in ‘tree and flesh.’
findings.scope: Annotate ¶8–¶9 as a mixed administrative-astrological quadrant scheme (four sides, guardian, leaders, plundering) that supplies asserted correspondences to categories of earthly affliction.

findings.diagnosis: Concluding recapitulation is coherent, but it contains a procedural/numerical justification (counting sun/moon) characteristic of later systematization. Still, it reads as a stitched conclusion to the present chapter and does not itself break narrative beyond the already-noted gloss in ¶6.
findings.evidence: These paragraphs are summary formulae (“Behold now, I have explained… Also, I have taught… I have recounted… Again, I have revealed…”), a common redactional cadence. ¶13’s rationale is bureaucratic/accounting: “counted in with them in relation to the calculation of the number,” and “constraint of the arrangement,” matching the spiritual reading’s observation of a “procedural rather than essential” reason. However, since it resolves the earlier question of inclusion and asserts “sun and the moon are from out of the greatness,” it functions as the chapter’s closure rather than a detachable intrusion.

textual_criticism.summary: 8 findings: 3 clean correspondential sections (¶2, ¶5, ¶7), 3 mixed seam/overlay diagnoses (¶3, ¶8–¶9, ¶10–¶13), 1 administrative overlay block (¶4), and 1 clear gloss intrusion (¶6). Recommendations: excise 2 (the five-world zodiac allocation in ¶3; the interrogative gloss in ¶6), annotate 2 (¶4; ¶8–¶9), none 4.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: Whether these twelve signs of the zodiac that are fixed on the sphere, or these five stars that circle upon them; those and these are rulers, all of them, according to their essence. They are all enemies and rivals to each other ⟨one oppresses another, they threaten each other⟩. They plunder one another by the action of the great craftsman who has formed all the worlds. He has gathered [them] and bound them on the sphere above, which circles constantly. Now, while it circles and tumbles them, so they shall do everything that they desire, above and below, according to their pleasure. Nevertheless, a guardian is over them, a debt-collector above them; compelling, extorting, and taking what is theirs away from them!

Now, this is how it can rightly be understood. These are the twelve rulers of depravity, the ones that wicked[ness] shall not [cease] For they cause all the evil and [disorder in the world]rld, whether in tree or in flesh.

⟨p.168⟩ And understand also about these five stars, the leaders: from where were they formed? The star of Zeus (Jupiter) was generated from the world of smoke, which is the mind. In contrast, Aphrodite (Venus) came about from the world of fire. And then Ares (Mars) belongs to the world of wind. Hermes (Mercury) belongs to the world of water. Cronos (Saturn) belongs to the world [of] Darkness.
And also, the two ascendants are counted to fire and desire, the dry and the moist. They are the father and the mother of all these.
And also, the sun and the moon, which are counted in with them as a rule so that they would reign over them. You will discover they subjugate them at every moment.

These seven we have named, the five stars and the two ascendants: They are the doers of wickedness that do every wicked and bad act in every land, the whole of it, above and below, in every creature, in the dry and the moist, in tree and flesh.

Once more I reveal to you about these signs of the zodiac: [They] are distributed, appointed on four sides, three per angle in these four places. And they are fixed to this revolving sphere. Aries, Leo and Sagittarius, they three belong to a single side. In contrast, Taurus, Capricorn and Virgo, these other three belong to another side. And then, Gemini, Libra and Aquarius belong to another side. Scorpio, Pisces and Cancer belong to another corner. Now, they are placed like this, appointed to these four parts, and distributed on the sphere.

So, when the side of Aries, Leo and Sagittarius will be plundered by the guardian who is over it, who extorts from it and the leaders who move upon it; at that instant shall affliction strike all the four-footed creatures below. However, when [the side] of Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn will be plundered; [affliction] shall ⟨p.169⟩ at once befall the herbs, together with the vegetables and all the fruits of the trees. Yet again, when the side of Scorpio, Pisces and Cancer will be plundered; scarcity shall befall the waters upon the earth, and drought be from place to place. Conversely, should the side of Gemini, Libra and Aquarius be plundered; deformity and stuntedness shall befall the form of mankind from place to place.
Behold now, I have explained to you about these twelve signs of the zodiac: They were fashioned from the five worlds of Darkness, and bound on the sphere.
Also, I have taught you about the other five, the stars: They too came about from the five worlds of the land of Darkness.
I have recounted to you also about the [t]wo ascendants: They are set to the mystery of fire and desire. They are the dry and the moist, the father and the mother.

Again, I have revealed to you about the sun and the moon: They are strangers to them. Still, because of the constraint of the arrangement, in that the thing receives light, and as they belong and plunder them; because of this they were counted in with them in relation to the calculation of the number. For, the sun and the moon are from out of the greatness, not belonging to the stars and the signs of the zodiac.

changes_summary: Implemented excisions per critic recommendations: (1) Finding 2—removed the five-world zodiac allocation catalogue from ¶3, retaining only the coherent framing and the functional conclusion about the twelve rulers and their effects, with minimal smoothing for prose continuity. (2) Finding 5—excised the intrusive interrogative gloss from ¶6, leaving the underlying statement about the sun and moon being counted in so they would reign and subjugate them. No other paragraphs were modified; items marked for annotation (Findings 3 and 7) were left unchanged per instructions.
